hints: Count the intersections of $y=f(x)$ with the horizontal line $y=k$.
Find the local maximum and minimum values and decide for which $k$ there are ${nr}$ intersections.
ca1_rootCountK.expl: The extreme values from $f'(x)=0$ are ${ext}$. Exactly ${nr}$ distinct roots occur when ${rng}$, so there are ${ans}$ integers $k$.

ca1_twoRootsK.prompt: For $f(x)={f}$, what is the sum of all real numbers $k$ for which $f(x)=k$ has exactly ${nr}$ distinct real roots? (digits only)
hints: The number of distinct roots changes when the horizontal line $y=k$ touches the graph at an extremum.
Use the shape of the graph to decide which touching cases give exactly ${nr}$ roots.
ca1_twoRootsK.expl: The extreme values are ${ext}$. Comparing the number of intersections at and around each extreme value, the valid $k$ are ${kk}$, and their sum is ${ans}$.

ca1_ineqParam.prompt: For $f(x)={f}$, what is the smallest real number $a$ such that $f(x)+a\ge 0$ holds for every $x$ in the interval ${dom}$? (digits only)
hints: $f(x)+a\ge0$ for all $x$ in the interval means the minimum of $f$ there is at least $-a$.
Find the minimum of $f$ by comparing the extreme values and the function values at the ends.
ca1_ineqParam.expl: The minimum of $f(x)$ on this interval is ${mn}$. The inequality always holds iff $a\ge {mn2}$, so the smallest $a$ is ${ans}$.

ca1_maxMinFind.prompt: The maximum of $f(x)={f}$ ($a$ a constant) on the closed interval $[{s},{t}]$ is ${M}$. What is the minimum on this interval? (digits only)
hints: On a closed interval, compare the extreme values inside it and the function values at both ends.
Find the maximum in terms of $a$ to determine $a$, then find the minimum the same way.
ca1_maxMinFind.expl: Comparing interior extreme values and the end values, the maximum is ${mx0}+a={M}$, so $a={av}$. The minimum is ${mn0}+a={ans}$.

ca1_optimBox.prompt: A rectangular sheet of paper is ${W}$ cm long and ${H}$ cm wide. Squares of equal size are cut from the four corners and the rest is folded into an open-top box. What is the maximum volume of the box, in cm³? (digits only)
hints: Let the side of each removed square be $x$ and write the volume as a function $V(x)$.
The maximum is at the root of $V'(x)=0$ with $0<x<(\text{shorter side})\div 2$.
ca1_optimBox.expl: With squares of side $x$ cm, $V(x)=x({W}-2x)({H}-2x)$ for $0<x<{hh}$; $V'(x)=0$ gives the maximum where $V$ changes from increasing to decreasing, at $x={x}$. The maximum volume is ${ans}$ cm³.

ca1_optimProfit.prompt: Producing and selling $x$ units a day ($0\le x\le {X}$) costs $C(x)={cost}$ (in ten-thousand won), and each unit sells for ${price}$ ten-thousand won. What is the maximum daily profit (sales minus cost), in ten-thousand won? (digits only)
hints: Write the profit as $P(x)=({price})x-C(x)$ and solve $P'(x)=0$.
Compare the value at the local maximum with the values at the ends $x=0$ and $x={X}$.
ca1_optimProfit.expl: $P(x)={price}x-C(x)$, and $P'(x)=0$ gives the local maximum at $x={xs}$ inside the interval. Comparing $P({xs})={ans}$, $P(0)={p0}$, $P({X})={pX}$, the maximum is ${ans}$.

ca1_velZeroAccel.prompt: A point P moves on a number line with position $x(t)={f}$ at time $t$ ($t\ge0$). What is its acceleration at the later of the two times at which its velocity is $0$? (digits only)
hints: Velocity is $v(t)=x'(t)$ and acceleration is $a(t)=v'(t)$.
Solve $v(t)=0$ for the two times, then substitute the later one into $a(t)$.
ca1_velZeroAccel.expl: $v(t)=x'(t)$ and $v(t)=0$ at $t={t1}$ and $t={t2}$. Substituting the later time $t={t2}$ into $a(t)=v'(t)$ gives ${ans}$.

ca1_kinCoefFind.prompt: A point P on a number line has position $x(t)={f}$ ($a$, $b$ constants). At $t={p}$ its velocity is $0$ and its acceleration is ${q}$. What is its position at $t={k}$? (digits only)
hints: Velocity is $x'(t)$ and acceleration is $x''(t)$; write $v({p})=0$ and $a({p})={q}$.
Solve the two equations for $a$ and $b$, then compute $x({k})$.

ca1_totalDistPos.prompt: A point P on a number line has position $x(t)={f}$ at time $t$ ($t\ge0$). How far does P travel from $t=0$ to $t={T}$? (digits only)
hints: Distance travelled is not the net change in position: split the interval where the direction reverses and add the lengths.
First find the times in $(0,{T})$ where $v(t)=x'(t)=0$.
ca1_totalDistPos.expl: Solving $v(t)=x'(t)=0$ shows the direction reverses at ${turns}$ within the interval. Splitting there and adding the absolute changes in position gives the distance ${ans}$.

ca1_throwImpact.prompt: A ball is thrown upward from a point ${h0}$ m above the ground, and its height after $t$ seconds is $h(t)={h}$ (m). What is the speed, in m/s, at the instant it hits the ground? (digits only)
hints: It hits the ground when $h(t)=0$ for a positive $t$. The velocity is $h'(t)$.
Solve for the positive root $t_0$ and compute $|h'(t_0)|$.
ca1_throwImpact.expl: The positive root of $h(t)=0$ is $t={T}$ s and $h'(t)={v0}-10t$, so $h'({T})={vv}$. Speed is the absolute value: ${ans}$ m/s.

ca1_indefInitial.prompt: A function $f$ has derivative $f'(x)={d}$ and $f({p})={q}$. What is $f({r})$? (digits only)
hints: $f(x)$ is an antiderivative of $f'(x)$; include the constant of integration $C$.
Use $f({p})={q}$ to fix $C$, then evaluate $f({r})$.

ca1_indefSecond.prompt: A function $f$ satisfies $f''(x)={d}$, $f'({p})={s}$ and $f({q})={w}$. What is $f({r})$? (digits only)
hints: Integrating $f''$ gives $f'$, integrating again gives $f$; each step adds a constant.
Use $f'({p})={s}$ for the first constant and $f({q})={w}$ for the second.
ca1_indefSecond.expl: Integrating $f''$ and using $f'({p})={s}$ gives $f'(x)={g1}$; integrating again and using $f({q})={w}$ gives $f(x)={g0}$. Hence $f({r})={ans}$.

ca1_defIntSymm.prompt: What is $\int_{-{a}}^{{a}}\left({g}\right)dx$? (a decimal, or a fraction such as 3/4, is fine)
hints: The interval is symmetric about $0$, so integrals of odd powers of $x$ vanish.
Keep the even-power terms and compute $2\int_0^{a}$.
ca1_defIntSymm.expl: Odd-power terms integrate to $0$ over $[-{a},{a}]$. The even-power terms give $2\int_0^{a}(\text{even part})\,dx={ansf}$.

ca1_defIntSplit.prompt: A continuous function $f$ satisfies $\int_{{a0}}^{{p}}f(x)\,dx={A}$ and $\int_{{a0}}^{{q}}f(x)\,dx={B}$. What is $\int_{{lo}}^{{hi}}\left({mf}\right)dx$? (digits only)
hints: Use $\int_a^b f\,dx+\int_b^c f\,dx=\int_a^c f\,dx$ and $\int_b^a f\,dx=-\int_a^b f\,dx$.
Express the integral of $f$ over the required interval through the two given values and integrate the constant part separately.
ca1_defIntSplit.expl: Over the required interval $\int f(x)\,dx={I}$. The constant term contributes $c\times(\text{signed length})$, and the total is ${ans}$.

ca1_integralEq.prompt: A polynomial $f$ satisfies $f(x)={rhs}$ for all real $x$. What is $f({k})$? (digits only)
hints: $\int_0^1 f(t)\,dt$ does not depend on $x$: call it $c$ and write $f(x)$ using $c$.
Substitute that $f$ into $\int_0^1 f(t)\,dt=c$ and solve for $c$.
ca1_integralEq.expl: Let $\int_0^1 f(t)\,dt=c$, a constant, so $f(x)$ is a quadratic containing $c$. Integrating it from $0$ to $1$ and equating with $c$ gives $c={c}$, and $f({k})={ans}$.

ca1_integralLimit.prompt: For the polynomial $f(x)={f}$, what is ${lim}$? (a decimal, or a fraction such as 3/4, is fine)
hints: Both numerator and denominator tend to $0$. Use $\frac{d}{d x}\int_a^x f(t)\,dt=f(x)$.
Write the integral as $F(\text{top limit})-F(\text{bottom limit})$ with $F'=f$; the limit becomes a derivative of $F$.
ca1_integralLimit.expl: With $F'=f$, writing the integral as $F(\text{top limit})-F(\text{bottom limit})$ turns the limit into a derivative of $F$, which equals ${ansf}$ in terms of values of $f$.

ca1_integralFuncFind.prompt: A polynomial $f$ satisfies $\int_{{c}}^{x}f(t)\,dt={F}$ ($a$ a constant) for all real $x$. What is $f({k})$? (digits only)
hints: At $x={c}$ the left side is $0$, which determines $a$.
Then differentiate both sides with respect to $x$ to get $f(x)$.
ca1_integralFuncFind.expl: At $x={c}$ the left side is $0$, so $a={av}$. Differentiating gives $f(x)={fx}$, hence $f({k})={ans}$.

ca1_integralFuncExtremum.prompt: For $f(t)={f}$, what is the local minimum value of $G(x)=\int_{{s}}^{x}f(t)\,dt$? (a decimal, or a fraction such as 3/4, is fine)
hints: $G'(x)=f(x)$, so monotonicity of $G$ is decided by the sign of $f(x)$.
$G$ has a local minimum where $f$ changes sign from $-$ to $+$; its value is $\int_{s}^{x}f(t)\,dt$ there.
ca1_integralFuncExtremum.expl: $G'(x)=f(x)$ changes sign from $-$ to $+$ at $x={z}$. The local minimum value is $G({z})=\int_{{s}}^{{z}}f(t)\,dt={ansf}$.

ca1_defIntAbs.prompt: What is $\int_{{p}}^{{q}}|{g}|\,dx$? (a decimal, or a fraction such as 3/4, is fine)
hints: Find the roots of the expression inside the absolute value that lie in the interval.
Split the interval there and remove the absolute value piece by piece with the correct sign.
ca1_defIntAbs.expl: The expression changes sign at $x={zs}$. Splitting the interval and removing the absolute value with the right sign on each part gives ${ansf}$.

ca1_defIntFindBound.prompt: For a positive number $a$, $\int_{{lo}}^{a}\left({g}\right)dx={V}$. What is $a$? (digits only)
hints: Find an antiderivative and write $\int_{{lo}}^{a}$ as a polynomial in $a$.
Solve the equation for $a>{lo}$; the expression is increasing there, so the root is unique.
ca1_defIntFindBound.expl: With the antiderivative $G(x)={G}$ we get $G(a)-G({lo})={V}$; for $a>{lo}$ the left side increases with $a$, so the root is unique. Solving gives $a={ans}$.

ca1_areaParabolaLine.prompt: What is the area of the region enclosed by the parabola $y={f}$ and the line $y={g}$? (a decimal, or a fraction such as 3/4, is fine)
hints: Solve the two equations simultaneously for the intersections $\alpha<\beta$.
Integrate (upper graph)−(lower graph) from $\alpha$ to $\beta$.
ca1_areaParabolaLine.expl: Solving simultaneously gives intersections at $x={al}$ and $x={be}$. Integrating (upper)−(lower) over this interval gives the area ${ansf}$.

ca1_areaCubicAxis.prompt: What is the total area of the two regions enclosed by the curve $y={f}$ and the $x$-axis? (a decimal, or a fraction such as 3/4, is fine)
hints: Find the $x$-intercepts (the three roots of the cubic).
On each part decide whether the curve is above or below the axis, and flip the sign where it is below.
ca1_areaCubicAxis.expl: The curve meets the $x$-axis at $x={rs}$. Integrating $|f(x)|$ over the two intervals and adding gives the total area ${ansf}$.

ca1_areaTangentParabola.prompt: What is the area of the region enclosed by the parabola $y={f}$, its tangent line at the point with $x$-coordinate ${a}$, and the $y$-axis? (a decimal, or a fraction such as 3/4, is fine)
hints: First find the tangent line; it lies entirely on one side of the parabola.
Integrate the absolute difference (parabola)−(tangent) from $x=0$ to $x={a}$.
ca1_areaTangentParabola.expl: The tangent line is $y={tl}$. Integrating the difference between the parabola and the tangent over the interval gives the area ${ansf}$.

ca1_areaLineParam.prompt: The curve $y={cur}$ and the line $y=mx$ ($0<m<{a}$) enclose a region of area ${S}$. What is the constant $m$? (digits only)
hints: The curve and the line meet at $x=0$ and $x={a}-m$.
Integrate (curve)−(line) between the intersections, write it in terms of $m$, and set it equal to ${S}$.
ca1_areaLineParam.expl: The intersections are $x=0$ and $x={a}-m$, and the area is $\int_0^{{a}-m}\{({a}-m)x-x^2\}dx=\frac{({a}-m)^3}{6}$. Setting this equal to ${S}$ gives ${a}-m={d}$, so $m={ans}$.

ca1_totalDistVel.prompt: A point P on a number line has velocity $v(t)={v}$ at time $t$ ($t\ge0$). How far does P travel from $t=0$ to $t={T}$? (a decimal, or a fraction such as 3/4, is fine)
hints: Distance travelled is the integral of the speed $|v(t)|$.
Split the interval at the times where $v(t)=0$ and integrate with the correct sign.
ca1_totalDistVel.expl: The velocity changes sign at ${zs}$ within the interval. Computing $\int_0^{T}|v(t)|\,dt$ piece by piece gives the distance ${ansf}$.

ca1_returnTime.prompt: A point P leaves the origin of a number line at $t=0$, and its velocity at time $t$ ($t\ge0$) is $v(t)={v}$. What is the velocity of P at the first time after the start when it is back at the origin? (digits only)
hints: Position is the antiderivative of velocity with $x(0)=0$: $x(t)=\int_0^t v(s)\,ds$.
Find the smallest positive $t$ with $x(t)=0$ and substitute it into $v(t)$.
ca1_returnTime.expl: $x(t)=\int_0^t v(s)\,ds={xt}$ and the positive solutions of $x(t)=0$ are ${rs}$. At the smallest, $t={t0}$, we get $v({t0})={ans}$.

pst_repPermCond.prompt: Using digits $0,\ 1,\ 2,\ \ldots,\ {m}$ with repetition allowed, we form ${k}$-digit natural numbers (the first digit is not $0$). How many of them contain the digit ${t}$ at least once? (digits only)
hints: 'At least once' is easier through the complement (the digit is never used). The first digit cannot be 0.
There are ${tot}$ ${k}$-digit natural numbers in all.
pst_repPermCond.expl: There are ${tot}$ such ${k}$-digit numbers in all, and ${noExpr}={no}$ of them never use the digit ${t}$. So ${tot}-{no}={ans}$.

pst_latticePath.prompt: On the coordinate plane, we move from $(0,\ 0)$ to $({m},\ {n})$ using only unit steps to the right or upward. How many shortest paths avoid the point $({p},\ {q})$? (digits only)
hints: Count all paths with permutations of repeated items. Avoiding = all - passing through.
Paths through $({p},\ {q})$ = (paths from the start to it) × (paths from it to the end).

pst_repCombEq.prompt: Count the ordered integer quadruples $(x,\ y,\ z,\ w)$ with $x+y+z+w={n}$, $x\ge {a}$, $y\ge {b}$, $z\ge {c}$ and $w\ge {d}$. (digits only)
hints: Put $x'=x-{a}$ and so on so that every variable is at least $0$.
The right-hand side of the new equation is ${m2}$.
pst_repCombEq.expl: With $x'=x-{a}$, $y'=y-{b}$, $z'=z-{c}$, $w'=w-{d}$ we get $x'+y'+z'+w'={m2}$ with non-negative integers. Combinations with repetition: $_{4}\mathrm{H}_{{m2}}=\binom{{m3}}{{m2}}={ans}$.

pst_monotoneSeq.prompt: For elements $a,\ b,\ c,\ d$ of the set $\{1,\ 2,\ \ldots,\ {m}\}$, how many ordered quadruples $(a,\ b,\ c,\ d)$ satisfy $a{r1}b{r2}c{r3}d$? (digits only)
hints: Wherever the sign is $<$ the two numbers must differ; shrink the range of available values accordingly.
With only $\le$ signs, choosing the four numbers is a combination with repetition.
pst_monotoneSeq.expl: There are ${s}$ signs $<$; subtracting $1$ successively from the later numbers turns all signs into $\le$ and the range becomes $1$ to ${ms}$. Choosing $4$ numbers with repetition from it gives $_{{ms}}\mathrm{H}_{4}=\binom{{top}}{4}={ans}$.

pst_binomCoef2.prompt: Find the coefficient of $x^{{k}}$ in the expansion of $({ax}{bs})^{{n}}$. (digits only)
hints: The general term of the binomial theorem has the form $\binom{N}{j}A^{N-j}B^{j}$.
Find the term in which $x$ is picked exactly $k$ times.
pst_binomCoef2.expl: The term picks the $x$-part ${k}$ times and the constant ${nk}$ times, so the coefficient is $\binom{{n}}{{k}}\cdot{a}^{{k}}\cdot({b})^{{nk}}={ans}$.

hints: In $(1+x)^{N}=\sum_{k=0}^{N}\binom{N}{k}x^{k}$ substitute a suitable value for $x$.
Substitute $x={a}$.

pst_binomUnknown.prompt: The coefficient of $x^{{k}}$ in the expansion of $(x+a)^{{n}}$ is ${V}$. Find the positive number $a$. (digits only)
hints: Write the coefficient of $x^{{k}}$ in terms of $a$.
Since $\binom{{n}}{{k}}={C}$, first find $a^{{nk}}$.
pst_binomUnknown.expl: The coefficient of $x^{{k}}$ is $\binom{{n}}{{k}}a^{{nk}}={C}a^{{nk}}$, so ${C}a^{{nk}}={V}$ and $a^{{nk}}={q}$. As $a>0$, $a={ans}$.

pst_diceSum.prompt: Two fair dice, each with faces $1$ to ${s}$, are thrown together and show $a$ and $b$. Find the probability that $a+b{rel}{t}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: Treating the dice as distinguishable, there are ${s}\times{s}$ equally likely outcomes.
For each $a$ from $1$ to ${s}$ count the values of $b$ that work, then add.
pst_diceSum.expl: There are ${tot}$ outcomes and ${cnt}$ of them satisfy the condition, so the probability is ${fe}$.

pst_diceQuad.prompt: A fair die with faces $1$ to ${s}$ is thrown twice, giving $a$ then $b$. Find the probability that the quadratic equation $x^{2}-{pa}x+{qb}=0$ has two distinct real roots. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: Two distinct real roots means the discriminant $D>0$.
$D=({pa})^{2}-4\times{qb}$; fix $a$ and count the values of $b$ that work.
pst_diceQuad.expl: The pairs $(a,\ b)$ with $D=({pa})^{2}-4\times{qb}>0$ number ${cnt}$ out of ${tot}$, so the probability is ${fe}$.

pst_atLeast.prompt: A bag holds ${w}$ white balls and ${bk}$ black balls. When ${k}$ balls are drawn at the same time, find the probability that at least ${r}$ of them are white. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: The complement of 'at least ${r}$ white' is 'at most ${rm1}$ white'.
The total number of ways to draw is $\binom{{nn}}{{k}}={tot}$.
pst_atLeast.expl: The complement is 'at most ${rm1}$ white', which has ${bad}$ ways. The total is $\binom{{nn}}{{k}}={tot}$, so the probability is $1-\frac{{bad}}{{tot}}={fr}$.

pst_lineUp.prompt: ${m}$ boys and ${w}$ girls stand in a line. Find the probability that no two girls stand next to each other. (You may count only the pattern of genders.) (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: Place the boys first; the girls go into the gaps between them or at the ends.
There are ${m1}$ possible places for the girls.
pst_lineUp.expl: The total number of gender patterns is $\binom{{nn}}{{w}}={tot}$. Choosing ${w}$ of the ${m1}$ gaps (between boys or at the ends) keeps girls apart: $\binom{{m1}}{{w}}={good}$. Probability ${fe}$.

pst_multiplesUnion.prompt: One card is drawn at random from ${N}$ cards numbered $1$ to ${N}$. Find the probability that the number is a multiple of ${p}$ or a multiple of ${q}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: Count the multiples of ${p}$ and of ${q}$ first. Multiples of both are multiples of the least common multiple.
|union| = (sum) - |intersection|.
pst_multiplesUnion.expl: There are ${np}$ multiples of ${p}$, ${nq}$ of ${q}$ and ${nl}$ multiples of the lcm ${l}$. So ${np}+{nq}-{nl}={cnt}$ and the probability is ${fe}$.

pst_deMorgan.prompt: For events $A,\ B$ with $P(A)={pa}$, $P(B)={pb}$ and $P(A\cap B)={pab}$, find $P({ev})$. (write it as a decimal)
hints: Draw a Venn diagram and split it into the four regions $A\cap B$, $A\cap B^{c}$, $A^{c}\cap B$, $A^{c}\cap B^{c}$.
$P(A\cap B^{c})=P(A)-P(A\cap B)$ and $P(A^{c}\cap B)=P(B)-P(A\cap B)$.
pst_deMorgan.expl: The four regions have probabilities $P(A\cap B)={pab}$, $P(A\cap B^{c})={ao}$, $P(A^{c}\cap B)={bo}$, $P(A^{c}\cap B^{c})={ne}$. $P({ev})$ is the sum of the regions it contains: ${sumx}$.

pst_condTable.prompt: A club has ${N}$ students: ${m}$ boys, ${g}$ students wearing glasses, and ${x}$ boys wearing glasses. A student chosen at random is found not to wear glasses. Find the probability that this student is a girl. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: Make a 2×2 table of boy/girl and glasses/no glasses and fill in all four cells.
In $P(B\mid A)=\frac{n(A\cap B)}{n(A)}$ the condition $A$ is 'no glasses'.
pst_condTable.expl: There are ${f}$ girls, of whom ${g}-{x}={gy}$ wear glasses, so ${f}-{gy}={fn}$ girls do not. Students without glasses: ${N}-{g}={ng}$. The probability is ${fe}$.

pst_condDice.prompt: Two distinguishable fair dice are thrown together, showing $a$ and $b$. Let $A$ be the event '$a+b{rel}{t}$' and $B$ the event '$a{relb}b$'. Find the conditional probability $P(B\mid A)$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: First list all outcomes belonging to $A$.
$P(B\mid A)=\frac{n(A\cap B)}{n(A)}$.

pst_indepUnknown.prompt: Events $A$ and $B$ are independent, with $P(A)={fa}$ and $P(A\cup B)={fu}$. Find $P(B)$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: Independence means $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$.
Rewrite the addition rule $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)$ as an equation for $P(B)$.
pst_indepUnknown.expl: By independence $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)$, i.e. $P(B)\{1-P(A)\}=P(A\cup B)-P(A)$. Here $1-{fa}={d1}$ and ${fu}-{fa}={d2}$, so $P(B)={d2}\div{d1}={fr}$.

pst_indepFindN.prompt: One card is drawn at random from $n$ cards numbered $1$ to $n$. Let $A$ be 'the number is a multiple of ${p}$' and $B$ 'the number is a multiple of ${q}$'. Among the integers $n$ with $2\le n\le {M}$, find the largest $n$ for which $A$ and $B$ are independent. (digits only)
hints: Independence means $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$, and $A\cap B$ is the set of multiples of ${l}$.
Check what happens when $n$ is a multiple of ${l}$.
pst_indepFindN.expl: If $n={l}t$ ($t$ a positive integer) then $P(A)=\frac{1}{{p}}$, $P(B)=\frac{1}{{q}}$, $P(A\cap B)=\frac{1}{{l}}$, so they are independent. The largest multiple of ${l}$ up to ${M}$ is ${ans}$, and no larger $n\le{M}$ gives independence (checked directly). The answer is ${ans}$.

pst_urnChain.prompt: A bag holds ${w}$ white and ${bk}$ black balls. Balls are drawn one at a time without replacement. Find the probability that the first ${r}$ draws are all white and draw number ${r1}$ is black. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: Multiplication rule: the number of balls left changes at every step.
The probability that the first ball is white is $\frac{{w}}{{nn}}$.
pst_urnChain.expl: Multiplying the conditional probabilities of each step: ${prod}={fr}$.

pst_totalProb.prompt: A fair die is thrown once. If the result is at most ${t}$, a ball is drawn from box A, otherwise from box B. Box A holds ${w1}$ white and ${b1}$ black balls; box B holds ${w2}$ white and ${b2}$ black balls. Find the probability that the ball drawn is white. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: A white ball comes either from A or from B.
Each part is (probability of choosing the box) × (probability of white in that box).
pst_totalProb.expl: White from A: $\frac{{t}}{6}\times{pw1}={tA}$; white from B: $\frac{{t6c}}{6}\times{pw2}={tB}$ (where $\frac{{t6c}}{6}$ is the probability of choosing B). The sum is ${fr}$.

pst_bayes.prompt: A fair die is thrown once. If the result is at most ${t}$, a ball is drawn from box A, otherwise from box B. Box A holds ${w1}$ white and ${b1}$ black balls; box B holds ${w2}$ white and ${b2}$ black balls. Given that the ball drawn is white, find the probability that it came from box A. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: $P(A\mid \text{white ball})=\frac{P(A\cap \text{white ball})}{P(\text{white ball})}$.
The denominator is P(white from A) + P(white from B).
pst_bayes.expl: P(white from A) = ${tA}$ and P(white from B) = ${tB}$, so the probability is $\frac{{tA}}{{tA}+{tB}}={fr}$.

pst_expectTable.prompt: A random variable $X$ takes the values $1,\ 2,\ \ldots,\ {n}$ with $P(X=x)=k(x+{c})$ for $x=1,\ 2,\ \ldots,\ {n}$ ($k$ is a constant). Find the mean $E(X)$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: Use the fact that the probabilities add up to $1$ to find $k$ first.
$E(X)=\sum x\,P(X=x)$.
pst_expectTable.expl: The probabilities sum to $1$: $k\sum_{x=1}^{{n}}(x+{c})={S1}k=1$, so $k=\frac{1}{{S1}}$. Then $E(X)=\frac{1}{{S1}}\sum_{x=1}^{{n}}x(x+{c})={fe}$.

pst_varTable.prompt: A random variable $X$ has $P(X={x1})=\frac{{a1}}{{d}}$, $P(X={x2})=\frac{{a2}}{{d}}$, $P(X={x3})=\frac{{a3}}{{d}}$. Find the variance $V(X)$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: First find $E(X)$ and $E(X^{2})$.

pst_linTransform.prompt: A random variable $X$ has mean ${m}$ and standard deviation ${s}$. For $Y={ya}$, find $E(Y^{2})$. (digits only)
hints: Use $E(Y)=aE(X)+b$ and $V(Y)=a^{2}V(X)$.

pst_binomFindN.prompt: A random variable $X$ follows the binomial distribution $B(n,\ p)$ with $E(X)={mu}$ and $V(X)={vr}$. Find $n$. (digits only)
hints: $E(X)=np$ and $V(X)=np(1-p)$.
Dividing $V(X)$ by $E(X)$ gives $1-p$.

pst_binomTail.prompt: A random variable $X$ follows the binomial distribution $B({n},\ {pf})$. Find $P(X{rel}{t})$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: $P(X=j)=\binom{N}{j}p^{j}(1-p)^{N-j}$ ($N$ = number of trials). If there are many terms to add, think of the complement.
Add the terms for $j=$ ${js}$.
pst_binomTail.expl: $P(X=j)=\binom{{n}}{j}\left({pf}\right)^{j}\left(1-{pf}\right)^{{n}-j}$, and the required probability is the sum of these for $j={js}$, namely ${fr}$.

pst_binomPmfEq.prompt: A random variable $X$ follows $B({n},\ p)$ and $P(X={r})=P(X={r1})$. Find $p$ (with $0<p<1$). (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: Write both probabilities as $\binom{N}{j}p^{j}(1-p)^{N-j}$ and cancel the common factors.
You obtain the value of $\frac{p}{1-p}$.

pst_bestOf.prompt: Teams A and B play until one of them has won ${w}$ games, and that team is the champion. A wins each game with probability ${fp}$, games are independent and there are no draws. Find the probability that A becomes champion. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: Split by the game in which A gets its ${w}$-th win.
To win in game ${w}+j$, A must have ${wm1}$ wins and $j$ losses in the previous ${wm1}+j$ games.
pst_bestOf.expl: A wins the series in game ${w}+j$ ($j=0,\ 1,\ \ldots,\ {wm1}$) with probability $\binom{{wm1}+j}{j}\left({fp}\right)^{{w}}\left(1-{fp}\right)^{j}$. Summing gives ${fr}$.

pst_normalBetween.prompt: A random variable $X$ follows the normal distribution $N({m},\ {s}^{2})$. Find $P({a}\le X\le {b})$. For a random variable $Z$ with the standard normal distribution, $P(0\le Z\le 0.5)=0.1915$, $P(0\le Z\le 1)=0.3413$, $P(0\le Z\le 1.5)=0.4332$, $P(0\le Z\le 2)=0.4772$, $P(0\le Z\le 2.5)=0.4938$, $P(0\le Z\le 3)=0.4987$. (write it as a decimal)
hints: Standardize with $Z=\frac{X-m}{\sigma}$ to get $P(z_1\le Z\le z_2)$.
The standard normal curve is symmetric about $Z=0$.

pst_normalFindParam.prompt: A random variable $X$ follows the normal distribution $N(m,\ {s}^{2})$ and $P(X\ge {c})={pv}$. Find the constant $m$. For a random variable $Z$ with the standard normal distribution, $P(0\le Z\le 0.5)=0.1915$, $P(0\le Z\le 1)=0.3413$, $P(0\le Z\le 1.5)=0.4332$, $P(0\le Z\le 2)=0.4772$, $P(0\le Z\le 2.5)=0.4938$, $P(0\le Z\le 3)=0.4987$. (digits only)
hints: Turn $P(X\ge {c})$ into a probability for $Z$ and compare it with $0.5$.
Find $z_0$ from the table value of $P(0\le Z\le z_0)$.
pst_normalFindParam.expl: $P(X\ge {c})=P\left(Z\ge \frac{{c}-m}{{s}}\right)={pv}$. From the table $P(0\le Z\le |z_0|)=|{pv}-0.5|={tv}$, so $|z_0|={az}$; if ${pv}<0.5$ then $z_0>0$, otherwise $z_0<0$, so $\frac{{c}-m}{{s}}={zz}$. Hence $m={ans}$.

pst_normalSymmetric.prompt: A random variable $X$ follows $N({m},\ {s}^{2})$ and $P(X\le {L})=P(X\ge {R})$. Find the constant $k$. (digits only)
hints: The normal curve is symmetric about the mean $m$.
The two values lie at equal distances on opposite sides of the mean, so they add up to $2m$.
pst_normalSymmetric.expl: The curve is symmetric about $x={m}$, so $({L})+({R})=2\times{m}$. This simplifies to ${A}k+({BD})={m2}$, giving $k={ans}$.

pst_binomNormal.prompt: A random variable $X$ follows the binomial distribution $B({n},\ {pf})$. Approximate $X$ by a normal distribution (no continuity correction) and find $P(X{rel}{r})$. For a random variable $Z$ with the standard normal distribution, $P(0\le Z\le 0.5)=0.1915$, $P(0\le Z\le 1)=0.3413$, $P(0\le Z\le 1.5)=0.4332$, $P(0\le Z\le 2)=0.4772$, $P(0\le Z\le 2.5)=0.4938$, $P(0\le Z\le 3)=0.4987$. (write it as a decimal)
hints: For large $n$, $B(n,\ p)$ is approximated by $N(np,\ np(1-p))$.
Standardize using the mean ${mu}$ and standard deviation ${sg}$.
pst_binomNormal.expl: $E(X)={mu}$ and $\sigma(X)=\sqrt{{vr}}={sg}$, so $X$ is approximately $N({mu},\ {sg}^{2})$. With $Z=\frac{X-{mu}}{{sg}}$ we get $\frac{{r}-{mu}}{{sg}}={z}$, so $P(X{rel}{r})\approx{expr}$.

pst_sampleSd.prompt: A population has mean ${m}$ and variance ${v}$. A random sample of size ${n}$ is taken and its sample mean is $\overline{X}$. Find $E(\overline{X}^{2})$. (write it as a decimal)
hints: $E(\overline{X})=m$ and $V(\overline{X})=\frac{\sigma^{2}}{{n}}$.
$E(\overline{X}^{2})=V(\overline{X})+\{E(\overline{X})\}^{2}$.

pst_sampleMeanNormal.prompt: A normal population has mean ${m}$ and standard deviation ${s}$. A random sample of size ${n}$ is taken, with sample mean $\overline{X}$. Find $P(\overline{X}{rel}{c})$. For a random variable $Z$ with the standard normal distribution, $P(0\le Z\le 0.5)=0.1915$, $P(0\le Z\le 1)=0.3413$, $P(0\le Z\le 1.5)=0.4332$, $P(0\le Z\le 2)=0.4772$, $P(0\le Z\le 2.5)=0.4938$, $P(0\le Z\le 3)=0.4987$. (write it as a decimal)
hints: $\overline{X}$ follows $N\left(m,\ \left(\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{{n}}}\right)^{2}\right)$.
Standardize using the standard deviation $\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{{n}}}={h}$.

pst_sampleMeanDist.prompt: A bag holds 3 balls, numbered ${lst}$ respectively. A ball is drawn, its number is noted and it is put back; this is done ${nt}$ times. Let $\overline{X}$ be the mean of the ${nt}$ noted numbers. Find $P(\overline{X}\ge {t})$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: Because the balls are replaced, all ordered outcomes are equally likely.
Count the ordered outcomes whose mean is at least ${t}$.
pst_sampleMeanDist.expl: There are ${tot}$ equally likely ordered outcomes, and ${cnt}$ of them have mean at least ${t}$. The probability is ${fe}$.

pst_stratified.prompt: The residents of a region form three groups A, B, C of ${na}$, ${nb}$ and ${nc}$ people. A sample is drawn by proportional stratified sampling (each group is sampled in proportion to its size), and ${sa}$ people are chosen from group A. How many people are chosen from group C? (digits only)
hints: With proportional allocation, the sampling fraction (sample ÷ group size) is the same in every group.
Find the fraction for group A first.
pst_stratified.expl: The sampling fraction in A is $\frac{{sa}}{{na}}$. It is the same in every group, so group C contributes ${nc}\times\frac{{sa}}{{na}}={ans}$ people.

pst_ciBounds.prompt: A random sample of size ${n}$ from a normal population with standard deviation ${s}$ has sample mean ${xb}$. The ${cl}\%$ confidence interval for the population mean $m$ is $a\le m\le b$. Find $b$. (Use $z={z}$ for the ${cl}\%$ level.) (write it as a decimal)
hints: The interval is $\overline{x}-z\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{{n}}}\le m\le \overline{x}+z\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{{n}}}$.
Since $\sqrt{{n}}={rt}$, first compute $\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{{n}}}$.

pst_ciSampleSize.prompt: A random sample is taken from a normal population with standard deviation ${s}$ to estimate the mean at the ${cl}\%$ confidence level. Find the smallest sample size $n$ for which the length of the confidence interval is at most ${L}$. (Use $z={z}$ for the ${cl}\%$ level; $n$ is a positive integer.) (digits only)
hints: The length of the interval is $2z\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}$.
Solve $2z\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}\le {L}$ for $\sqrt{n}$, then square.
pst_ciSampleSize.expl: The length $2\times{z}\times\frac{{s}}{\sqrt{n}}\le {L}$ gives $\sqrt{n}\ge\frac{2\times{z}\times{s}}{{L}}$, so $n\ge\left(\frac{2\times{z}\times{s}}{{L}}\right)^{2}\approx{nq}$. The smallest positive integer is ${ans}$.

ca2_seqLimit.prompt: Find the limit of the sequence. $\lim_{n\to\infty}{ex}$ (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Divide numerator and denominator by the highest power of $n$ in the denominator, or rationalize first if there are radicals.
Terms like $\frac{1}{n}$ and $\frac{1}{n^{2}}$ tend to $0$ as $n\to\infty$.
ca2_seqLimit.expl: Simplifying and letting $n\to\infty$ gives ${wk}$, so the limit is ${res}$.

ca2_seqGeoLimit.prompt: Find the limit. $\lim_{n\to\infty}{ex}$ (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: The power with the largest base decides the limit.
Divide numerator and denominator by it; the terms with smaller bases tend to $0$.
ca2_seqGeoLimit.expl: Divide the numerator and denominator by the term with the largest absolute base, ${dom}$: the remaining coefficient ratio is ${wk}$, so the limit is ${res}$.

ca2_geoConvCount.prompt: Find the number of integers $x$ for which the sequence $\left\{\left({rt}\right)^{n}\right\}$ converges. (digits only)
hints: A geometric sequence $\{r^{n}\}$ converges only when $-1<r\le 1$.
Solve the inequality that puts the expression for $r$ in this range.
ca2_geoConvCount.expl: The convergence condition $-1<r\le 1$ gives ${rg}$. The integers $x$ satisfying it are ${lst}$, so there are ${ans}$ of them.

ca2_seqSumLimit.prompt: Find the limit. $\lim_{n\to\infty}{ex}$ (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: The sum $\sum_{k=1}^{n}k^{p}$ is a polynomial in $n$ with leading term $\frac{n^{p+1}}{p+1}$.
Only the leading coefficients matter.
ca2_seqSumLimit.expl: Write the sum as a polynomial in $n$ and compare leading coefficients: ${wk}$, so the limit is ${res}$.

ca2_partialSumSeries.prompt: The sum of the first $n$ terms of a sequence $\{a_n\}$ is $S_n=\frac{{sa}}{{sb}}$. Find ${ask}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: $a_1=S_1$, and $a_n=S_n-S_{n-1}$ for $n\ge 2$.
The sum of an infinite series is the limit of its partial sums $S_n$.

ca2_telescope.prompt: Find the sum of the infinite series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}{term}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: If the two factors in the denominator differ by a constant, split into partial fractions.
In the partial sums most terms cancel and only the first few remain.
ca2_telescope.expl: Splitting into partial fractions and cancelling in the partial sums leaves ${wk}$, so the sum is ${res}$.

ca2_geoSeriesParam.prompt: The infinite series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}{term}$ converges and its sum is ${S}$. Find the constant $r$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: The sum of an infinite geometric series is (first term)÷(1-ratio).
Identify the first term and the common ratio from the general term.
ca2_geoSeriesParam.expl: The first term is ${fa}$ and the ratio is ${ratio}$, so the sum is ${sumf}={S}$. Solving gives $r={res}$.

ca2_ballDistance.prompt: A ball is dropped from a height of ${h}$ m. Each time it hits the floor it bounces up to ${ratio}$ times the height it just fell from, then falls again, and this repeats forever. What is the total distance the ball travels, in m? (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Treat the first drop of ${h}$ m separately from the later up-and-down trips (each is twice the height reached).
The heights reached form a geometric sequence whose first term is (initial height)×(bounce ratio).
ca2_ballDistance.expl: The heights reached add up to ${up}$ m and every up-and-down trip is twice that, so the total is ${h}+2\times {up}={res}$ m.

ca2_expLogLimit.prompt: Find the limit. $\lim_{{to}}{ex}$ (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Use $\lim_{x\to0}\frac{e^{x}-1}{x}=1$ and $\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\ln(1+x)}{x}=1$ after rewriting the expression.
Multiply and divide by suitable constants so the same expression appears in numerator and denominator.
ca2_expLogLimit.expl: Rewriting to use the basic limits gives ${wk}$, so the limit is ${res}$.

ca2_eExponent.prompt: If $\lim_{{to}}{ex}=e^{k}$, find $k$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Aim for the form $\lim_{h\to0}(1+h)^{\frac{1}{h}}=e$.
Multiply and divide the exponent so that it is the reciprocal of the added term $h$.
ca2_eExponent.expl: Using $(1+h)^{\frac{1}{h}}\to e$ and collecting the exponent gives $k={wk}={res}$.

ca2_derivExpLog.prompt: For $f(x)={fx}$, find $f'({x0})$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Differentiate with $(e^{x})'=e^{x}$, $(\ln x)'=\frac{1}{x}$ and the chain rule.
If the value substituted has the form $\ln m$, use $e^{\ln m}=m$.

ca2_quotientDeriv.prompt: For $f(x)={fx}$, find $f'({x0})$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Use the quotient rule $\left(\frac{u}{v}\right)'=\frac{u'v-uv'}{v^{2}}$.
Evaluate $u$, $v$, $u'$, $v'$ at $x={x0}$ and substitute.

ca2_trigLimit.prompt: Find the limit. $\lim_{{to}}{ex}$ (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Use $\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin x}{x}=1$, $\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\tan x}{x}=1$ and $1-\cos x=\frac{\sin^{2}x}{1+\cos x}$.
For $x\to c$, put $t=x-c$ and let $t\to0$.
ca2_trigLimit.expl: Rewriting with the basic limits gives ${wk}$, so the limit is ${res}$.

ca2_trigLimitUnknown.prompt: Find the positive integer $a$ for which ${eq}$ holds. (digits only)
hints: Express the limit as $x\to0$ in terms of $a$.
Set that expression equal to the given value and solve for $a$.
ca2_trigLimitUnknown.expl: The limit equals ${wk}$, which must equal the given value, so $a={ans}$.

ca2_limitPair.prompt: For constants $a$ and $b$, if ${eq}$, find $ab$. (digits only)
hints: The denominator tends to $0$ while the limit exists, so the numerator must also tend to $0$.
Expand the numerator in powers of $x$ and cancel the lowest-order terms first.

ca2_trigDeriv.prompt: For $f(x)={fx}$, find $f'({x0})$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Use $(\sin x)'=\cos x$, $(\cos x)'=-\sin x$, the product rule and the chain rule to find $f'(x)$.
Substitute $x={x0}$ and evaluate the trigonometric values.

ca2_addTheorem.prompt: Given ${ga}$, ${gb}$, ${ra}$ and ${rb}$, find ${ask}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Use the given value and $\sin^{2}\theta+\cos^{2}\theta=1$ to get the other values; the quadrant decides the signs.
Substitute the values into the addition formula.

ca2_lineAngle.prompt: The acute angle between the lines $ {l1} $ and $ {l2} $ is $\theta$. Find $\tan\theta$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: A line of slope $m$ makes an angle $\alpha$ with the positive $x$-axis where $\tan\alpha=m$.
Use the tangent subtraction formula and take the positive value because the angle is acute.

ca2_doubleAngle.prompt: If ${cd}$, find ${ask}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Use $\sin2\alpha=2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha$, $\cos2\alpha=\cos^{2}\alpha-\sin^{2}\alpha$ and $\sin^{2}\alpha+\cos^{2}\alpha=1$.
Try squaring the given relation, or get $\sin$ and $\cos$ from the value of $\tan$.

ca2_chainTable.prompt: For differentiable functions $f$ and $g$, ${tbl}$. If $h(x)={hx}$, find $h'({a})$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Decide whether $h$ is a product, a quotient or a composite and use the matching rule.
Read the needed values and derivatives at $x={a}$ (and at the inner values) from the data.

ca2_paramDeriv.prompt: For the curve $x={xt}$, $y={yt}$, find ${what}$ at $t={t0}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: For parametric functions, $\frac{ dy }{ dx }=\frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}$.
The second derivative is $\frac{d}{ dt }\left(\frac{ dy }{ dx }\right)$ divided by $\frac{ dx }{ dt }$.

ca2_implicitDeriv.prompt: Treating $y$ as a function of $x$, find ${what}$ at the point $ {pt} $ of the curve ${eq}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Differentiate both sides with respect to $x$; terms containing $y$ pick up a factor $\frac{ dy }{ dx }$.
Substitute the coordinates of the point and solve for $\frac{ dy }{ dx }$.

ca2_inverseDeriv.prompt: Let $g$ be the inverse function of $f(x)={fx}$. Find $g'({b})$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: First find $a$ with $f(a)={b}$.
Inverse function rule: $g'({b})=\frac{1}{f'(a)}$.
ca2_inverseDeriv.expl: Since $f({xa})={b}$ we have $g({b})={xa}$, and $f'(x)={fp}$ gives $f'({xa})={fd}$. Hence $g'({b})=\frac{1}{f'({xa})}={res}$.

ca2_tangentLine.prompt: Find the $y$-coordinate of the point where the tangent line to the curve ${cv}$ at the point $ {pt} $ meets the $y$-axis. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: The derivative at the point of tangency is the slope of the tangent line.
Put $x=0$ into $y-y_0=m(x-x_0)$.
ca2_tangentLine.expl: The point of tangency is $ {pt} $ and the slope is $m={sl}$, so the tangent is $y={tl}$ and its $y$-intercept is ${res}$.

ca2_tangentTriangle.prompt: Find the area of the triangle bounded by the tangent line to the curve ${cv}$ at the point $ {pt} $ and the $x$-axis and $y$-axis. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Find the tangent line first, then its intercepts with the two axes.
The base and height of the triangle are $|x\text{-intercept}|$ and $|y\text{-intercept}|$.
ca2_tangentTriangle.expl: The tangent line is $y={tl}$ with $x$-intercept ${xi}$ and $y$-intercept ${yi}$, so the area is $\frac{1}{2}\times|{xi}|\times|{yi}|={res}$.

ca2_commonTangent.prompt: The curves $y={f}$ and $y={g}$ meet at the point with $x=1$ and have a common tangent line there. For the constants $a$ and $b$, find $ab$. (digits only)
hints: Meeting at $x=1$ means $f(1)=g(1)$; having the same tangent means $f'(1)=g'(1)$.
Solve the two equations for $a$ and $b$.

ca2_extremaPair.prompt: The function $f(x)={fx}$ has exactly one local maximum and one local minimum. If the local maximum is at $x=\alpha$ and the local minimum is at $x=\beta$, find $\alpha-\beta$. (digits only)
hints: Find where $f'(x)=0$ and see how the sign of $f'(x)$ changes around those points.
A sign change of $f'$ from positive to negative gives a local maximum; negative to positive gives a local minimum.
ca2_extremaPair.expl: $f'(x)={fp}$, so the local maximum is at $x={mx}$ and the local minimum at $x={mn}$. Hence $\alpha-\beta=({mx})-({mn})={ans}$.

ca2_rootCount.prompt: Find the number of distinct real roots of the equation ${eq}$. (digits only)
hints: Call the left side $f(x)$ and count the intersections of the curve $y=f(x)$ with the line $y=k$, where $k$ is the constant on the right.
Study where $f$ increases and decreases, find its extreme values and its behaviour as $x\to\pm\infty$, then compare $k$ with those values.
ca2_rootCount.expl: From ${fpx}$ the extreme values are ${ext}$ and the limits are ${lim}$. Here ${cm}$, so the curve $y=f(x)$ and the line $y=k$ meet in {ans} point(s), and the equation has {ans} real root(s).

ca2_monotoneParam.prompt: Find the number of integers $a$ for which $f(x)={fx}$ is increasing on all real numbers. (It is increasing when $f'(x)\ge 0$ for every real $x$.) (digits only)
hints: A differentiable function is increasing on all of $\mathbb{R}$ exactly when $f'(x)\ge0$ for every $x$.
Find the range of $a$ for which the minimum of $f'(x)$ (or the discriminant) allows this, then count the integers.
ca2_monotoneParam.expl: ${wk}$. So the integers $a$ satisfying the condition are ${lst}$, in total {ans}.

ca2_motionReverse.prompt: A point P moves on a number line and its position at time $t$ ($t>0$) is $x(t)={xt}$. Find its acceleration at the first time its velocity is $0$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Velocity is $v(t)=x'(t)$ and acceleration is $a(t)=v'(t)$.
Find the smallest positive $t$ with $v(t)=0$ and substitute it into $a(t)$.
ca2_motionReverse.expl: ${wk}$, so the acceleration at the first time the velocity is zero is ${res}$.

ca2_riemann.prompt: If $L=\lim_{n\to\infty}{pre}\sum_{k=1}^{n}{body}$, find ${ask}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Read the sum as a sum of rectangle areas over $n$ equal parts and replace $\frac{k}{n}$ by $x$.
The limits of integration come from the values of $\frac{k}{n}$ at the ends, in the limit.
ca2_riemann.expl: Converting the sum to a definite integral gives $L={wk}$. Hence ${ask}$ equals ${res}$.

ca2_areaCurves.prompt: Let $S$ be the area of the region bounded by the graphs $y={f}$, $y={g}$ and the lines $x={a}$, $x={b}$. Find ${ask}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Integrate (upper graph) minus (lower graph) over the interval.
Use antiderivatives of exponential, trigonometric and rational functions.
ca2_areaCurves.expl: On $[{a},{b}]$ the graph $y={f}$ lies above, so $S=\int_{{a}}^{{b}}({f}-{gg})\,dx={wk}$. Hence ${ask}$ equals ${res}$.

ca2_volumeRotate.prompt: Let $V$ be the volume of the solid obtained by rotating about the $x$-axis the region bounded by the graphs $y={f}$, $y={g}$ and the lines $x={a}$, $x={b}$. Find ${ask}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: The volume is $V=\pi\int_{\alpha}^{\beta}\{(\text{outer radius})^{2}-(\text{inner radius})^{2}\}\,dx$.
Take the upper graph as the outer radius and the lower graph as the inner radius.

ca2_integralBasic.prompt: Let $I=\int_{{lo}}^{{hi}}\left({fx}\right)dx$. Find ${ask}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Use $\int e^{x}dx=e^{x}$, $\int\sin x\,dx=-\cos x$, $\int\cos x\,dx=\sin x$, $\int\frac{1}{x}dx=\ln|x|$.
Remember $\int f(kx)\,dx=\frac{1}{k}F(kx)$; then substitute the upper and lower limits and subtract.

ca2_substitution.prompt: Evaluate $\int_{{lo}}^{{hi}}{fx}\,dx$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Let $u$ be the inner part of the integrand; then $du$ matches the remaining factor.
Remember that the limits of integration change into values of $u$.

ca2_subsTransform.prompt: For a continuous function $f$, ${gv}$. Find ${tg}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Let $u$ be the inner expression and change the limits and $dx$ into the variable $u$.
Check that the new limits are the same as those of the given integral.

ca2_partsFormula.prompt: The function $f$ is differentiable with continuous $f'$, and ${given}$. Find ${tg}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: Integration by parts: $\int_{a}^{b}u\,v'\,dx=\left[uv\right]_{a}^{b}-\int_{a}^{b}u'\,v\,dx$.
Take $f'(x)$ as $v'$ and the other factor as $u$.

ca2_partsEval.prompt: Let $I=\int_{{lo}}^{{hi}}{fx}\,dx$. Find ${ask}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: In the product, let $u$ be the factor that gets simpler when differentiated and $v'$ the one that is easy to integrate; then integrate by parts.
Do it twice if necessary. Evaluate the trigonometric values at the ends of the interval.

ca2_velocityIntegral.prompt: A point P moves on a number line and its velocity at time $t$ ($t\ge0$) is $v(t)={vt}$. Let $x(t)$ be its position and $x(0)={x0}$. Find ${ask}$. (a decimal is fine, or a fraction written like 3/4)
hints: The change in position is $\int_{0}^{T}v(t)\,dt$, and the distance travelled is the integral of the speed $|v(t)|$.
Find where the velocity changes sign and split the interval there.

geo_parFocusDir.prompt: A parabola has focus $F({fx},\ {fy})$ and directrix ${dirEq}$. A point $P(x,\ y)$ on the parabola satisfies ${cond}$. What is the maximum value of ${un}$? (digits only)
hints: A point of a parabola is equally far from the focus and from the directrix.
The vertex is the midpoint between focus and directrix. Write the equation of the parabola with vertex $({vx},\ {vy})$ and $p={pp}$ first.
geo_parFocusDir.expl: The vertex is $({vx},\ {vy})$ and $p={pp}$, so the parabola is ${eqn}$. Substituting ${cond}$ gives ${un}={sol}$, so the maximum of ${un}$ is ${ans}$.

geo_parFocalChord.prompt: A line with slope ${m}$ passes through the focus of the parabola ${eq}$ and meets the parabola at P and Q. What is the length of segment PQ? (digits only)
hints: For a point of a parabola, the distance to the focus equals the distance to the directrix.
Substitute the equation of the line into the parabola and find the sum of the ${w}$-coordinates of the two intersection points.
geo_parFocalChord.expl: Since $p={pp}$, the focus is ${foc}$ and the line is ${line}$. Substituting gives ${w}_1+{w}_2={sum}$ for the ${w}$-coordinates, and by the directrix property $PQ=({w}_1+{pp})+({w}_2+{pp})={sum}+{twop}={ans}$.

geo_ellipseFocal.prompt: Let F and F' be the foci of the ellipse ${eq}$. A point P on the ellipse satisfies ${cond}$. What is the value of ${ask}$? (digits only)
hints: For a point on an ellipse the sum of the distances to the two foci is constant and equals the length of the major axis.
The semi-major axis is $a={a}$ and $c={c}$. Use $PF+PF'=2a$.
geo_ellipseFocal.expl: The semi-major axis is $a={a}$ and $c={c}$, so $PF+PF'=2a={tw}$ and $FF'=2c={tc}$. ${work}$, so the value is ${ans}$.

geo_hyperFocal.prompt: Let F and F' be the foci of the hyperbola ${eq}$. A point P on the hyperbola satisfies ${cond}$. What is the value of ${ask}$? (digits only)
hints: For a point on a hyperbola, the absolute difference of the distances to the foci equals the length $2a$ of the transverse axis.
Here $a={a}$ and $c={c}$, so $|PF-PF'|=2a={tw}$, and a point of the hyperbola is at least $c-a={ca}$ away from each focus.
geo_hyperFocal.expl: Here $a={a}$, $b={b}$, $c={c}$, $|PF-PF'|=2a={tw}$ and $FF'=2c={tc}$. ${work}$, so the value is ${ans}$.

geo_ellipseFromEq.prompt: What is the distance between the two foci of the ellipse ${eq}$? (digits only)
hints: Rewrite the ellipse as $\frac{x^2}{\square}+\frac{y^2}{\square}=1$; the larger denominator is $a^2$.
The two denominators are ${a2}$ and ${b2}$, and $c^2=a^2-b^2$.
geo_ellipseFromEq.expl: In the form ${std}$ we have $a^2={a2}$, $b^2={b2}$, so $c^2=a^2-b^2={c2}$ and $c={c}$. The distance between the foci is $2c={ans}$.

geo_hyperAsym.prompt: What is the slope of the asymptote with positive slope of the hyperbola ${eq}$? (decimal or fraction such as 3/4)
hints: The asymptotes of $\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ are $y=\pm\frac{b}{a}x$, and those of $\frac{y^2}{a^2}-\frac{x^2}{b^2}=1$ are $y=\pm\frac{a}{b}x$.
First rewrite it with right-hand side 1, ${std}$, and read off $a^2$ and $b^2$.
geo_hyperAsym.expl: In the form ${std}$ the asymptotes are ${asy}$, so the asymptote with positive slope has slope ${ans}$.

geo_eccentric.prompt: The curve ${eq}$ has eccentricity ${e}$, and ${cond}$. What is the value of $k$? (digits only)
hints: For both ellipse and hyperbola $e=\frac{c}{a}$. First decide which denominator is $a^2$.
Write $e^2$ in terms of $k$: for an ellipse $e^2=1-\frac{b^2}{a^2}$, for a hyperbola $e^2=1+\frac{b^2}{a^2}$.

geo_conicTangentLine.prompt: The line ${ln}$ is tangent to the curve ${eq}$. What is the positive value of $k$? (digits only)
hints: Substitute the line into the equation of the curve to get a quadratic in $x$; tangency means its discriminant is $0$.
Obtain an equation for $k$ from $D=0$.
geo_conicTangentLine.expl: Substituting the line into the curve gives a quadratic whose discriminant $D$ must be $0$ for tangency. ${work}$, so the positive $k$ is ${ans}$.

geo_tangentAt.prompt: What is the area of the triangle bounded by the tangent line to the curve ${eq}$ at the point $P({x0},\ {y0})$ and the $x$-axis and $y$-axis? (decimal or fraction such as 3/4)
hints: The tangent at $(x_1,\ y_1)$ is obtained by replacing $x^2\to x_1x$ and $y^2\to y_1y$ (for a parabola $y^2\to y_1y$ and $x\to\frac{x+x_1}{2}$).
Find the $x$- and $y$-intercepts of the tangent and compute $\frac{1}{2}\times|x\text{-intercept}|\times|y\text{-intercept}|$.
geo_tangentAt.expl: The tangent is ${tan}$ with $x$-intercept ${xi}$ and $y$-intercept ${yi}$. So the area is $\frac{1}{2}\times|{xi}|\times|{yi}|={ans}$.

geo_tangentsFromPoint.prompt: Two tangent lines to the curve ${eq}$ are drawn from the point $({x1},\ {y1})$. What is the product of their slopes? (decimal or fraction such as 3/4)
hints: Let the slope be $m$ and substitute the line ${lnp}$ through the point $({x1},\ {y1})$ into the equation of the curve.
The tangency condition (discriminant $=0$) gives a quadratic in $m$ whose two roots are the slopes of the tangents.
geo_tangentsFromPoint.expl: The slopes $m$ are the two roots of the quadratic ${quad}=0$ obtained from the tangency condition $D=0$. By Vieta, the product of the slopes is ${prod}$.

geo_chordMidpoint.prompt: The midpoint of the segment PQ joining two distinct points P and Q of the curve ${eq}$ is $M({x0},\ {y0})$. What is the slope of the line PQ? (decimal or fraction such as 3/4)
hints: Write the points as $(x_1,\ y_1)$, $(x_2,\ y_2)$; the midpoint tells you $x_1+x_2$ and $y_1+y_2$.
Substitute both points into the equation of the curve and subtract the two equations to get $\frac{y_1-y_2}{x_1-x_2}$.
geo_chordMidpoint.expl: Let $P(x_1,\ y_1)$, $Q(x_2,\ y_2)$. Then $x_1+x_2={sx}$ and $y_1+y_2={sy}$. Substituting both points into the curve and subtracting gives ${rel}$, so the slope is $\frac{y_1-y_2}{x_1-x_2}={sl}$.

geo_ellipseRightTri.prompt: Let F and F' be the foci of the ellipse ${eq}$. A point P on the ellipse satisfies $\angle FPF'=90^\circ$. What is the area of triangle PFF'? (digits only)
hints: By the definition $PF+PF'=2a$, and since the angle at P is right, $PF^2+PF'^2=(FF')^2$.
Use $(PF+PF')^2=PF^2+PF'^2+2\,PF\cdot PF'$ to find $PF\cdot PF'$.
geo_ellipseRightTri.expl: Here $a^2={a2}$, $b^2={b2}$, $c^2={c2}$, so $PF+PF'=2a={tw}$ and $FF'=2c={tc}$. Then $PF^2+PF'^2={tc2}$, so $2\,PF\cdot PF'=({tw})^2-{tc2}$, that is $PF\cdot PF'={pr}$. The area is $\frac{1}{2}\times PF\times PF'={ans}$.

geo_conicLattice.prompt: How many points on the curve ${eq}$ have both coordinates integers? (digits only)
hints: First bound the possible values of $x$ (or $y$), then try the integers one by one.
By symmetry of the curve, points that differ only in signs come together.
geo_conicLattice.expl: Checking the integers $x$, $y$ one by one, the points are ${sols}$, so there are ${ans}$ of them.

geo_conicGeneral.prompt: Consider the conic ${eq}$. Let $(a,\ b)$ be its focus with the largest $x$-coordinate (the focus itself if there is only one). What is $a+b$? (digits only)
hints: Complete the square in $x$ and in $y$ to reach the standard form.
Read the center (or vertex) from the standard form and move by $c$ (by $p$ for a parabola) along the axis to reach the focus.
geo_conicGeneral.expl: Completing the squares gives ${std}$. The focus is ${foc}$, so $a+b={ans}$.

geo_parMinSum.prompt: Let F be the focus of the parabola ${eq}$ and let A be the point $({xa},\ {ya})$. As the point P moves on the parabola, what is the minimum value of $PA+PF$? (digits only)
hints: For P on the parabola, the distance $PF$ equals the distance from P to the directrix.
If H is the foot of the perpendicular from P to the directrix, $PA+PH$ is smallest when A, P and H are collinear.
geo_parMinSum.expl: The directrix is ${dir}$. The point A lies inside the parabola (${chk}$), so with H the foot of the perpendicular from P to the directrix, the minimum of $PA+PF=PA+PH$ is the distance from A to the directrix, ${ans}$.

geo_ellipseExtSum.prompt: The ellipse ${eq}$ has a focus $F({fx},\ {fy})$, and the point $A({xa},\ {ya})$ lies inside the ellipse. As the point P moves on the ellipse, what is the product of the maximum and the minimum of $PA+PF$? (digits only)
hints: If F' is the other focus, $PF=2a-PF'$, so $PA+PF=2a+(PA-PF')$.
By the triangle inequality $-AF'\le PA-PF'\le AF'$, and both equalities occur because A is inside the ellipse.
geo_ellipseExtSum.expl: With F' the other focus, $PA+PF=2a+(PA-PF')$, where $a={a}$ and $AF'={dd}$. Since $-AF'\le PA-PF'\le AF'$, the maximum is $2a+AF'={mx}$, the minimum is $2a-AF'={mn}$, and the product is ${ans}$.

geo_spaceDist.prompt: What is the distance between the points $A{pa}$ and $B{pb}$ in space? (digits only)
hints: Find the three coordinate differences first.

geo_divPoint.prompt: For the points $A{pa}$ and $B{pb}$ in space, the point P lies on segment AB with $AP:PB={m}:{n}$. What is the sum of the three coordinates of P? (digits only)
hints: The point dividing AB internally in the ratio $m:n$ is $\left(\frac{mx_2+nx_1}{m+n},\ \frac{my_2+ny_1}{m+n},\ \frac{mz_2+nz_1}{m+n}\right)$.
Compute each coordinate separately.
geo_divPoint.expl: $P=\left(\frac{{n}\,x_A+{m}\,x_B}{{mn}},\ \frac{{n}\,y_A+{m}\,y_B}{{mn}},\ \frac{{n}\,z_A+{m}\,z_B}{{mn}}\right)={pp}$, so the sum of the coordinates is ${ans}$.

geo_divRatioPlane.prompt: For the points $A{pa}$ and $B{pb}$ in space, the segment AB meets the plane ${pl}$ at the point P. If $AP:PB=m:n$ with $m$, $n$ coprime positive integers, what is $m+n$? (digits only)
hints: A point of the plane ${pl}$ has one coordinate equal to $0$.
Write that coordinate of the point dividing AB internally in the ratio $s:t$ in terms of $s$ and $t$ and set it equal to $0$.
geo_divRatioPlane.expl: Let $AP:PB=s:t$. The relevant coordinate of P is $\frac{t\cdot({za})+s\cdot({zb})}{s+t}=0$, so $s:t=|{za}|:|{zb}|={ua}:{ub}$. In lowest terms this is ${m}:{n}$, so $m+n={ans}$.

geo_sphereExpand.prompt: The equation ${eq}$ represents a sphere of radius ${rad}$. What is the constant $s$? (digits only)
hints: Complete the square in $x$, $y$ and $z$ to reach $(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2+(z-c)^2=r^2$.
The right-hand side must equal $r^2={rad2}$.
geo_sphereExpand.expl: Completing the squares gives ${std}$. The squared radius is ${s4}-s={rad2}$, so $s={s4}-{rad2}={ans}$.

geo_sphereSection.prompt: The cross-section of the sphere ${eq}$ by the plane ${pl}$ is a circle of area $m\pi$. What is the natural number $m$? (digits only)
hints: Read the center and the squared radius from the equation.
If $d$ is the distance from the center to the plane, the radius $r$ of the circle satisfies $r^2=R^2-d^2$.
geo_sphereSection.expl: The center is ${cc}$ and $R^2={rr2}$. The distance from the center to the plane ${pl}$ is $d={dd}$, so the circle has $r^2={rr2}-{dd}^2={ans}$ and its area is ${ans}\pi$.

geo_sphereTangentPlane.prompt: The plane ${pl}$ is tangent to the sphere with center $C{cc}$ and radius ${rad}$. What is the larger value of the constant $k$? (digits only)
hints: Tangency means the distance from the center to the plane equals the radius.
The distance from $(x_0,\ y_0,\ z_0)$ to the plane $ax+by+cz=k$ is $\frac{|ax_0+by_0+cz_0-k|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}}$.
geo_sphereTangentPlane.expl: The normal vector $({nv})$ has length ${nn}$, and substituting the center into the left side gives ${dc}$. From $\frac{|{dc}-k|}{{nn}}={rad}$ we get $|{dc}-k|={rl}$, so $k={dc}\pm{rl}$, and the larger value is ${ans}$.

geo_vecLinComb.prompt: For $\vec a={va}$ and $\vec b={vb}$, what is $|{ex}|$? (digits only)
hints: Sums and scalar multiples of vectors are computed component by component.
Find the components of ${ex}$ first, then the square root of the sum of squares.

geo_vecDecompose.prompt: For $\vec a={va}$, $\vec b={vb}$, $\vec c={vc}$, real numbers $m$, $n$ satisfy $\vec c=m\vec a+n\vec b$. What is the value of ${ask}$? (decimal or fraction such as 3/4)
hints: Write the components of $m\vec a+n\vec b$ in terms of $m$ and $n$ and equate them with those of $\vec c$.
Solve the simultaneous equations for $m$ and $n$ obtained from two components.
geo_vecDecompose.expl: Comparing components gives ${eqs}$, so $m={mt}$ and $n={nt}$. Hence ${ask}={ans}$.

geo_dotNormExpand.prompt: For vectors $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ with $|\vec a|={na}$, $|\vec b|={nb}$ and $\vec a\cdot\vec b={dt}$, what is $|{ex}|^2$? (digits only)
hints: Since $|\vec x|^2=\vec x\cdot\vec x$, expand the dot product of ${ex}$ with itself.
Express it with $|\vec a|^2$, $|\vec b|^2$ and $\vec a\cdot\vec b$ and substitute.

geo_dotFromNorms.prompt: For vectors $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ with $|\vec a|={na}$, $|\vec b|={nb}$ and $|{ex}|={uu}$, what is $\vec a\cdot\vec b$? (digits only)
hints: Expand $|{ex}|^2$ in terms of $|\vec a|^2$, $|\vec b|^2$ and $\vec a\cdot\vec b$.
Substituting the given lengths gives a linear equation in $\vec a\cdot\vec b$.

geo_dotAngle.prompt: Let $\theta$ ($0^\circ\le\theta\le180^\circ$) be the angle between $\vec a={va}$ and $\vec b={vb}$. How many degrees is $\theta$? (digits only)
hints: The cosine of the angle is $\cos\theta=\frac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec a||\vec b|}$.
Compute the dot product and the two lengths.
geo_dotAngle.expl: $\vec a\cdot\vec b={dt}$ and $|\vec a||\vec b|=\sqrt{{na2}}\sqrt{{nb2}}$, so $\cos\theta={cs}$. For $0^\circ\le\theta\le180^\circ$ this gives $\theta={ans}^\circ$.

geo_vecOrthoParam.prompt: For vectors $\vec a={va}$ and $\vec b={vb}$, what is the largest real number $t$ with $\vec a\cdot\vec b={dd}$? (digits only)
hints: Multiply the components and add to write $\vec a\cdot\vec b$ as an expression in $t$.
Solve the resulting equation for all $t$ and pick the largest.
geo_vecOrthoParam.expl: $\vec a\cdot\vec b={dexp}$, so solving ${dexp}={dd}$ gives ${sol}$. The largest value is ${ans}$.

geo_vecCircleEq.prompt: Let $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ be the position vectors of the points $A{pa}$ and $B{pb}$, and let $\vec p$ be the position vector of a point P. The points P satisfying $(\vec p-\vec a)\cdot(\vec p-\vec b)=0$ form a circle or a sphere. What is its radius? (decimal or fraction such as 3/4)
hints: $(\vec p-\vec a)\cdot(\vec p-\vec b)=0$ says that the vectors $\vec p-\vec a$ and $\vec p-\vec b$ are perpendicular.
So the angle subtended by AB at P is a right angle, and AB is a diameter.
geo_vecCircleEq.expl: $(\vec p-\vec a)\cdot(\vec p-\vec b)=0$ means P lies on the circle (sphere) with diameter AB. Since $AB={ab}$, the radius is $\frac{1}{2}AB={ans}$.

geo_lineIntersectParam.prompt: The two lines ${l1}$ and ${l2}$ in space meet in a point. What is the value of the constant $k$? (digits only)
hints: Call the common values of the two lines $s$ and $t$ and write the points of each line using $s$ and $t$.
Solve for $s$ and $t$ from the equal $x$- and $y$-coordinates, then compare the $z$-coordinates.
geo_lineIntersectParam.expl: Let $s$ and $t$ be the common values of the first and second line. The $x$- and $y$-coordinates must agree: ${xy}$, which gives $s={ss}$, $t={tt}$. The $z$-coordinates must agree: ${eq3}$, so $k={ans}$.

geo_lineSpacePoint.prompt: A point on the line ${ln}$ satisfies ${cond}$. What is the sum of its other two coordinates? (digits only)
hints: Let the common value of the three fractions be $s$; then $x$, $y$ and $z$ can all be written with $s$.
Use the given condition ${cond}$ to find $s$ first.
geo_lineSpacePoint.expl: Let the common value be $s$; then $(x,\ y,\ z)=({par})$. From ${cond}$ we get $s={ss}$, so the point is ${pt}$ and the sum of the other two coordinates is ${ans}$.

geo_lineVec2D.prompt: In the coordinate plane the point A has coordinates $({x1},\ {y1})$. The line through A with direction vector $\vec u=({u1},\ {u2})$ meets the line ${ln}$ at the point $(a,\ b)$. What is $a+b$? (digits only)
hints: A point of the line through A with direction $\vec u$ has the form $(x,\ y)=A+t\vec u$.
Substitute its coordinates into the equation ${ln}$ and solve for $t$.
geo_lineVec2D.expl: The points of the line are $(x,\ y)=({par})$. Substituting into ${ln}$ gives ${eqn}$, so $t={tt}$. The intersection is ${pt}$, hence $a+b={ans}$.

geo_planeNormal.prompt: For the point $A{pa}$, the plane through A perpendicular to the vector $\vec n=({vn})$ meets the ${ax}$-axis at a point. What is its ${ax}$-coordinate? (decimal or fraction such as 3/4)
hints: For a point P of the plane with position vector $\vec p$, $\vec n\cdot(\vec p-\vec a)=0$.
First find the plane $ax+by+cz=d$; a point of the ${ax}$-axis has its other two coordinates equal to $0$.
geo_planeNormal.expl: For P on the plane $\vec n\cdot(\vec p-\vec a)=0$, so the plane is ${plane}$. On the ${ax}$-axis the other two coordinates are $0$, so ${solve}$ and the ${ax}$-coordinate is ${ans}$.

geo_projPlaneArea.prompt: A figure of area ${ar}$ lies in the plane ${pl}$. What is the area of its orthogonal projection onto the ${cp}$-plane? (digits only)
hints: If $\theta$ is the angle between the plane of the figure and the ${cp}$-plane, the projected area is (area)$\times\cos\theta$.
The angle between two planes equals the angle between their normal vectors, so find $\cos\theta$ from the normals.
geo_projPlaneArea.expl: The plane ${pl}$ has normal vector $({nv})$ of length ${nn}$. The cosine with the normal of the ${cp}$-plane is $\cos\theta=\frac{{ni}}{{nn}}$, so the projected area is ${ar}\times\frac{{ni}}{{nn}}={ans}$.

geo_projEllipse.prompt: A circle of radius ${rr}$ lies in the plane $\alpha$, and its orthogonal projection onto the plane $\beta$ is an ellipse. Let $\theta$ be the angle between the planes, with $\cos\theta={cs}$. What is the distance between the two foci of this ellipse? (digits only)
hints: The diameter parallel to the line of intersection keeps its length, and the perpendicular one shrinks by the factor $\cos\theta$.
Find the semi-axes of the projected ellipse and compute $c=\sqrt{a^2-b^2}$.
geo_projEllipse.expl: The projected ellipse has semi-major axis $a={rr}$ and semi-minor axis $b={rr}\cos\theta={bb}$. Then $c=\sqrt{{rr}^2-{bb}^2}={cc}$, so the distance between the foci is $2c={ans}$.

geo_threePerp.prompt: From a point P outside the plane $\alpha$, the foot of the perpendicular to $\alpha$ is H. From H the foot of the perpendicular to a line $\ell$ in $\alpha$ is K, and A is a point of $\ell$ different from K. If ${giv}$, what is the length of segment ${ask}$? (digits only)
hints: Since $PH\perp\alpha$ and $HK\perp\ell$, the three perpendiculars theorem gives $PK\perp\ell$.
Apply the Pythagorean theorem in the resulting right triangles one after another.
geo_threePerp.expl: Since $PH\perp\alpha$ and $HK\perp\ell$, the three perpendiculars theorem gives $PK\perp\ell$. ${work}$, so the length is ${ans}$.

econ_exchangeCross.prompt: The exchange rates are 1 dollar $={d}$ won and 1 euro $={e}$ won. Without any fee, how many dollars do you get for ${n}$ euros? (digits only)
hints: First find what ${n}$ euros are worth in won.
Then divide that amount of won by the price of one dollar, ${d}$ won.

econ_taxBracket.prompt: An income tax splits the taxable income into brackets with different rates: ${r1}$% on the part up to ${b1}$ (ten-thousand won), ${r2}$% on the part above ${b1}$ up to ${b2}$, and ${r3}$% on the part above ${b2}$. For a taxable income of ${x1}$ (ten-thousand won), how much tax is due, in ten-thousand won? (digits only)
hints: Each rate applies only to the amount lying inside its bracket. Find the amount in each bracket first.
Add (amount in the bracket)×(rate) over all brackets.
econ_taxBracket.expl: The amounts in the brackets are ${s1}$, ${s2}$ and ${s3}$, so the tax is ${s1}\times\frac{{r1}}{100}+{s2}\times\frac{{r2}}{100}+{s3}\times\frac{{r3}}{100}={ans}$ (ten-thousand won).

econ_compoundFV.prompt: ${P}$ won is deposited for ${n}$ years in an account with annual rate ${r}$% that adds interest to the principal ${m}$ times a year. The rate for one compounding period is the annual rate divided by ${m}$, and nothing is withdrawn. What is the total amount (principal plus interest) after ${n}$ years, in won? (Drop any fraction of a won. Digits only.)
hints: The number of compounding periods is (times per year)×(number of years).
With the per-period rate ${rp}$%, the total is the principal times $(1+\frac{{rp}}{100})$ multiplied once per period.
econ_compoundFV.expl: There are ${m}\times{n}={k}$ periods at ${rp}$% each, so the total is ${P}\times(1+\frac{{rp}}{100})^{{k}}\approx{ex}$ won; dropping the fraction gives ${ans}$ won.

econ_presentValue.prompt: Interest is compounded once a year at an annual rate of ${r}$%. What is the present value of ${F}$ won to be received ${n}$ years from now, in won? (Drop any fraction of a won. Digits only.)
hints: The present value $P$ is the amount that grows to ${F}$ won in ${n}$ years with compound interest.
Compute $P=F\div(1+\frac{{r}}{100})^{{n}}$.
econ_presentValue.expl: $P={F}\div(1+\frac{{r}}{100})^{{n}}\approx{ex}$ won; dropping the fraction gives ${ans}$ won.

econ_annuityPV.prompt: An annuity pays ${A}$ won at the end of each year for ${n}$ years (the first payment in 1 year, the last in ${n}$ years). With an annual rate of ${r}$% compounded yearly, what is the present value of the annuity, in won? (Drop any fraction of a won. Digits only.)
hints: Discount each payment back to today for as many years as it is delayed, then add them.
With $i=\frac{{r}}{100}$ the present value is $A\times\frac{1-(1+i)^{-{n}}}{i}$.
econ_annuityPV.expl: With $i={r}/100$ the present value is ${A}\times\frac{1-(1+i)^{-{n}}}{i}\approx{ex}$ won; dropping the fraction gives ${ans}$ won.

econ_taxEquilibrium.prompt: The demand curve of a good is $p={a}-{b}q$ and its supply curve is $p={c}+{d}q$, where $p$ is the price (won) and $q$ the quantity. The government charges the seller a tax of ${t}$ won for every unit sold, so the seller receives the price paid by the consumer minus the tax. At the new equilibrium after the tax, what price does the consumer pay, in won? (digits only)
hints: The price the seller actually receives is $p-{t}$.
Put $p-{t}$ in place of $p$ in the supply curve and substitute $p={a}-{b}q$ to find $q$.
econ_taxEquilibrium.expl: The seller receives $p-{t}$, so $({a}-{b}q)-{t}={c}+{d}q$. Solving gives $q={qn}$, and the consumer pays $p={a}-{b}\times{qn}={ans}$ won.

econ_equilibriumTable.prompt: The quantity demanded of a good is ${qd1}$ when the price is ${p1}$ won and ${qd2}$ when it is ${p2}$ won; the quantity supplied is ${qs1}$ when the price is ${p3}$ won and ${qs2}$ when it is ${p4}$ won. If both quantities are linear functions of the price, what is the equilibrium price at which they are equal, in won? (digits only)
hints: Use the slope of the line through two points to see how each quantity changes with price.
Call the quantities $Q_d$ and $Q_s$ and find the price where $Q_d=Q_s$.
econ_equilibriumTable.expl: The demand changes at the rate $\frac{{qd2}-{qd1}}{{p2}-{p1}}={md}$, so $Q_d={qd1}{md}(p-{p1})$; supply changes at the rate ${ns}$, so $Q_s={qs1}+{ns}(p-{p3})$. Setting $Q_d=Q_s$ gives $p={ans}$ won.

econ_utilityBundle.prompt: Good x costs ${a}$ won per unit and good y costs ${b}$ won per unit. You spend the whole budget of ${I}$ won exactly on $x$ units of good x and $y$ units of good y ($x$, $y$ are integers at least 0). If the utility is $U={U}$, what is the maximum utility? (digits only)
hints: Find all integer pairs $(x, y)$ with $x,y\ge0$ satisfying the budget equation ${a}x+{b}y={I}$.
Compute $U$ for each pair and compare.
econ_utilityBundle.expl: The pairs satisfying the budget equation are ${pairs}$. The largest $U$ occurs at $(x, y)=({bx}, {by})$, where $U={ans}$.

econ_regionLP.prompt: A factory makes $x$ units of product A and $y$ units of product B ($x$, $y$ are integers at least 0). One unit needs ${a1}$ kg of material and ${t1}$ hours of work for product A, and ${b1}$ kg and ${t2}$ hours for product B. At most ${M}$ kg of material and ${T}$ hours of work are available per day. The profit is ${pa}$ (ten-thousand won) per unit of A and ${pb}$ per unit of B. What is the maximum daily profit, in ten-thousand won? (digits only)
hints: Write the conditions as inequalities, together with $x\ge0$ and $y\ge0$, and draw the region in the plane.
The profit ${pa}x+{pb}y$ is largest at a vertex of the region. Check the intersection of the two boundary lines first.
econ_regionLP.expl: The inequalities are ${a1}x+{b1}y\le{M}$, ${t1}x+{t2}y\le{T}$, $x\ge0$, $y\ge0$. The profit is largest at the vertex where the two boundary lines meet, $({x0}, {y0})$, which is a lattice point, so the maximum profit is ${pa}\times{x0}+{pb}\times{y0}={ans}$.

econ_leontief.prompt: Two industries 1 and 2 have the input coefficient matrix $A={M}$ (the $(i, j)$ entry is the amount of industry $i$'s product needed to make one unit of industry $j$'s product). Let the total outputs be $x_1$, $x_2$ (unit: 100 million won) and the final demands $d_1={d1}$, $d_2={d2}$; then ${XV}=A{XV}+{DV}$. What is $x_1$? (digits only)
hints: Rewrite the equation as $(I-A){XV}={DV}$.
Find the inverse of $I-A$ and multiply it by ${DV}$. The inverse of a $2\times2$ matrix is $\frac{1}{ad-bc}$ times a rearranged matrix.
econ_leontief.expl: From $(I-A)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{d}$ we get $\mathbf{x}=(I-A)^{-1}\mathbf{d}$. The determinant of $I-A$ is ${D}$, so $x_1=\frac{{c22}\times{d1}+{a12}\times{d2}}{{D}}={ans}$.

econ_inverseEntry.prompt: What is the $({i}, {j})$ entry of the inverse $A^{-1}$ of the matrix $A={M}$? (The $(i, j)$ entry is in row $i$, column $j$.) (a decimal or a fraction like 3/4 is fine)
hints: The determinant of ${G}$ is $ad-bc$; the inverse exists if it is not 0.
The inverse is ${H}$.
econ_inverseEntry.expl: The determinant is ${a}\times{d}-({b})\times({c})={det}$, and the $({i}, {j})$ entry of $A^{-1}$ is $\frac{{num}}{{det}}$, that is ${fr}$.

econ_marginalRevenue.prompt: The demand curve of a good is $p={a}-{b}q$ ($p$ is the price in won, $q$ the quantity sold). Total revenue is $R(q)=pq$ and marginal revenue is the derivative $R'(q)$. For what quantity $q$ is the marginal revenue equal to ${m}$ won? (digits only)
hints: Substitute $p={a}-{b}q$ into $R(q)=pq$ to write $R(q)$ in terms of $q$.
Differentiate $R(q)$ and find $q$ so that the derivative equals ${m}$.

econ_elasticityPoint.prompt: The demand function is $q={D}$ ($p$ is the price, $q$ the quantity demanded). What is the price elasticity of demand $e=\left|q'(p)\times\frac{p}{q}\right|$ at the price $p={p0}$? (a decimal or a fraction like 3/4 is fine)
hints: First find $q'(p)$ and evaluate it at $p={p0}$.
Also find the quantity $q$ at $p={p0}$ and put both into the formula for $e$.

econ_elasticityUnit.prompt: For the demand function $q={D}$, at what price $p$ is the price elasticity $e=\left|q'(p)\times\frac{p}{q}\right|$ equal to 1? (Consider only $p>0$ with quantity $q>0$.) (digits only)
hints: Find $q'(p)$ and write $\left|q'(p)\times\frac{p}{q}\right|=1$ as an equation in $p$.
For $q>0$ we have $q'(p)<0$, so removing the absolute value gives $-q'(p)\times p=q$.
econ_elasticityUnit.expl: $q'(p)={dq}$, so $-q'(p)\times p=q$ gives ${eqn}$, and the solution with $p>0$ is $p={ans}$.

econ_profitCubic.prompt: Producing $q$ units of a product costs $C(q)=q^3-{b}q^2+{c}q+{f}$ won in total, and the selling price is a constant ${p}$ won per unit. If everything produced is sold, what is the maximum profit (total revenue minus total cost), in won? ($q$ is a real number at least 0.) (digits only)
hints: The profit is $\pi(q)={p}q-C(q)$. Differentiate and find $q$ with $\pi'(q)=0$.
At the positive root of $\pi'(q)=-3q^2+{twob}q+{pc}=0$, the sign of $\pi'(q)$ changes from + to -.
econ_profitCubic.expl: $\pi(q)={p}q-C(q)$ gives $\pi'(q)=-3q^2+{twob}q+{pc}=-3(q-{q0})(q+{s})$. For $q\ge0$, $\pi'$ is positive before $q={q0}$ and negative after, so the maximum is at $q={q0}$: $\pi({q0})={ans}$ won.

ai_cosine.prompt: The word-frequency vectors of documents A and B (counts of the dictionary words, in dictionary order) are $\vec{a}={va}$ and $\vec{b}={vb}$. What is their cosine similarity $\dfrac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|}$? (a decimal or a fraction such as 3/4 is fine)
hints: First compute the dot product by multiplying matching entries and adding.
A length is the square root of the sum of squared entries; both lengths are whole numbers.

ai_jaccard.prompt: The dictionary words are numbered $1$ to $12$. The word numbers appearing in document A form the set $A=\{{sa}\}$ and in document B the set $B=\{{sb}\}$. What is the Jaccard similarity $\dfrac{n(A\cap B)}{n(A\cup B)}$ of the two documents? (a decimal or a fraction such as 3/4 is fine)
hints: $A\cap B$ is the set of word numbers appearing in both documents.
$n(A\cup B)=n(A)+n(B)-n(A\cap B)$.
ai_jaccard.expl: $n(A\cap B)={ni}$ and $n(A\cup B)={nu}$, so the similarity is $\frac{{ni}}{{nu}}={fr}$.

ai_jaccardRev.prompt: Document A contains ${na}$ distinct words and document B contains ${nb}$. For their word sets $A$ and $B$ the Jaccard similarity $\dfrac{n(A\cap B)}{n(A\cup B)}$ equals $\dfrac{{jp}}{{jq}}$. How many distinct words appear in both documents? (digits only)
hints: Let $x$ be the number of common words; then $n(A\cup B)=n(A)+n(B)-x$.
Solve $\dfrac{x}{{na}+{nb}-x}=\dfrac{{jp}}{{jq}}$ for $x$.
ai_jaccardRev.expl: Since $n(A\cup B)={na}+{nb}-x$, we need $\frac{x}{{na}+{nb}-x}=\frac{{jp}}{{jq}}$, which gives $x={ans}$.

ai_pixelBright.prompt: The brightness values (0-255) of the pixels of a grayscale image form the matrix $A={mat}$. To brighten the image every pixel value $p$ is replaced by $\min(255,\ {a}p+{b})$ (values above 255 become 255). What is the sum of all entries of the new matrix? (digits only)
hints: Compute ${a}p+{b}$ for each entry first, then cap it at 255.
Write the whole new matrix, then add all its entries.
ai_pixelBright.expl: The new matrix is $B={res}$ and the sum of all its entries is ${ans}$.

ai_flipTranspose.prompt: The brightness values of a $3\times4$ image form the matrix $A={mat}$. Reversing the order of the entries in every row (a left-right flip) gives the matrix $B$, and the transpose of $B$ is $C$. What is the entry of $C$ in row {i}, column {j}? (digits only)
hints: First write each row of $A$ backwards to get $B$.
The transpose swaps rows and columns, so $C$ is a $4\times3$ matrix.
ai_flipTranspose.expl: $B={bm}$ and $C={cm}$, so the entry in row {i}, column {j} is ${ans}$.

ai_convolve.prompt: A filter $K={ker}$ is applied to the image $I={img}$ by sliding it one cell at a time. At each position the overlapping entries are multiplied and added, and these values form a feature map. What is the sum of all entries of the feature map? (digits only)
hints: With the filter on the top-left corner, multiply overlapping entries and add: that is the first entry of the map.
Move the filter one cell right or down and repeat.
ai_convolve.expl: The feature map is ${out}$ and the sum of its entries is ${ans}$.

ai_bayesSpam.prompt: ${s}\%$ of the received e-mails are spam. ${p}\%$ of the spam e-mails contain a certain word, and ${q}\%$ of the non-spam e-mails contain it too. An e-mail containing this word is chosen. What is the probability that it is spam? (a decimal or a fraction such as 3/4 is fine)
hints: Imagine $100$ (or $10000$) e-mails and count each case.
It is (spam containing the word) divided by (all e-mails containing the word).
ai_bayesSpam.expl: Out of $10000$ e-mails, ${s2}$ are spam and ${a}$ of them contain the word; of the ${h2}$ non-spam e-mails, ${b}$ contain it. So the probability is $\frac{{a}}{{a}+{b}}={fr}$.

hints: Find the means $\bar{x}$ and $\bar{y}$. The trend line passes through $(\bar{x},\bar{y})$.
The slope is $a=\dfrac{\sum(x_i-\bar{x})(y_i-\bar{y})}{\sum(x_i-\bar{x})^2}$.

ai_mseLoss.prompt: For the points {pts}, what is the mean squared error (MSE) $\dfrac{1}{n}\sum(y_i-\hat{y}_i)^2$ of the line model $\hat{y}={model}$? (digits only)
hints: First find the error $y_i-\hat{y}_i$ at every point.
Square the errors, add them and divide by the number of points $n={np}$.
ai_mseLoss.expl: The errors are ${res}$ and the sum of squares is ${sq}$, so the MSE is $\frac{{tot}}{{np}}={ans}$.

ai_gradStep.prompt: The loss function $L(w)={lw}$ is reduced by gradient descent: $w_{n+1}=w_n-\eta L'(w_n)$ with learning rate $\eta={eta}$ and starting value $w_0={w0}$. What is $w_{{t}}$ after {t} updates? (digits only)
hints: First find $L'(w)$.
Compute $w_1$, $w_2$, ... in turn starting from $w_0$.

ai_gradMse.prompt: The model $\hat{y}=wx$ predicts the points {pts}. The loss is $L(w)=\dfrac{1}{n}\sum(wx_i-y_i)^2$ ($n$ is the number of points). Starting at $w_0={w0}$ with learning rate $\eta={eta}$, apply one gradient-descent step $w_1=w_0-\eta L'(w_0)$. What is $w_1$? (digits only)
hints: $L'(w)=\dfrac{2}{n}\sum x_i(wx_i-y_i)$.
Put in $w=w_0$ to get the slope $L'(w_0)$ first.

job_flowUnits.prompt: A water dispenser nozzle delivers ${r}$ mL of water per minute at a constant rate. If it is kept open for ${h}$ hours ${m}$ minutes, how many litres of water come out in total? (1 L = 1000 mL. Digits only.)
hints: Convert the whole time into minutes.
Multiply (amount per minute)×(minutes) to get mL, then divide by 1000 to get L.
job_flowUnits.expl: The time is ${h}\times60+{m}={tot}$ minutes, so ${r}\times{tot}={ml}$ mL come out. ${ml}\div1000={ans}$ L.
